# batches
FCT-004 [rule|batches] Batch numbers are recorded only for scheduled drugs (from evt_004) | conf 0.90 | stated | quote: "batch numbers only for scheduled drugs"
# business
FCT-001 [context|business] We make a stock tool for small pharmacy shops (from evt_001) | conf 0.90 | stated | quote: "we are building a stock tool for small pharmacy shops"
# expiry
FCT-003 [rule|expiry] The tool warns when a medicine is within 60 days of its expiry date (from Q-003) | conf 0.90 | stated | quote: "warn me when a medicine is within sixty days of expiry"
# network
FCT-005 [constraint|network] Shops often have weak internet, so the tool must keep working offline for a day (from evt_005) | conf 0.90 | stated | consumers: blueprint,frontend,qa | quote: "the internet is weak in many shops, it must work offline for a day"
# reorder
FCT-006 [requirement|reorder] In version one the tool only prepares a low-stock list and does not send orders to wholesalers (from Q-006) | conf 0.90 | stated | quote: "for now just make the low stock list, don't send orders to the wholesaler"
FCT-007 [preference|reorder] The owner reads the low-stock list every morning (from evt_007) | conf 0.90 | stated | quote: "I look at the low stock list every morning"
# users
FCT-002 [role|users] The shop owner and one assistant use it (from evt_002) | conf 0.90 | stated | consumers: blueprint,screens | quote: "the owner and one assistant use it"

needs.label: Your idea in one line
needs.sufficient: One or two sentences that say what the app does and for whom, in the user's own words.

needs.label: Roles
needs.sufficient: Each distinct kind of person who signs in: their top goal and what they can approve or change.

needs.label: Features
needs.sufficient: What each feature is for (the job it does) and what must be in the first release.

needs.label: What it must not do
needs.sufficient: Anything the app must explicitly not do or include.

needs.label: Offline use
needs.sufficient: Whether the app must work without internet, and which parts.

kinds.description: A business rule, policy or functional requirement the app must follow or enforce.
A quantity, limit, price, percentage, duration or other figure the app depends on.
A condition that must hold for a feature to count as done.
A screen, page or view and what it shows or lets the person do.
A sequence of steps a person goes through to get something done.
A thing the app keeps track of (a record, a document, an item) and what is known about it.
A law, regulation, consent, privacy or certification requirement.
A quality the app must have (speed, offline use, security, accessibility, reliability, scale).
An outside system, service or interface and how the app uses it.
A limit on how the app is built or run (budget, deadline, platform, must use, must not).
A sample case, number or situation that illustrates how something should work.
A taste, style or wish that is not a hard requirement.
Background about the business, the people, the place or the goal.
A detail that fits none of the kinds above; every agent may need it.

output.summary: A stock tool for small pharmacy shops with expiry warnings and a morning low-stock list.
output.pitch: Small pharmacy shops get a stock tool that warns the owner when a medicine is close to expiry and prepares a low-stock list every morning. It keeps working for a day without internet, and in version one it does not send orders to wholesalers.
